results.title: Standard temperature and pressure - Wikipedia
excerpts:
* Until 1982, STP was defined as a temperature of 273.15 K (0.00 °C ; 32.00 °F ) and an absolute pressure of exactly 1 standard atmosphere (101,325.000 Pa ) .
* Since 1982, STP has still been defined as a temperature of 273.15 K (0.00 °C; 32.00 °F) but defined with an absolute pressure of exactly 1 bar (100,000.000 Pa) .
IUPAC also defines SATP (Standard Ambient Temperature and Pressure) as a temperature of 298.15 K (25.00 °C ; 77.00 °F ) and an absolute pressure of exactly 1 atm (101.325 kPa) . [ 3 ]
NIST uses a temperature of 20 °C (293.15 K; 68.00 °F) and an absolute pressure of 1 atm (101.325 kPa) .
[ 4 ] This standard is also called normal temperature and pressure (abbreviated as NTP ). However, a common temperature and pressure in use by NIST for thermodynamic experiments is 298.15 K (25.00 °C; 77.00 °F) and 1 bar (100.000 kPa) .
[ edit ]
Before 1918, many professionals and scientists using the metric system of units defined the standard reference conditions of temperature and pressure for expressing gas volumes as being 15 °C (288.15 K ; 59.00 °F ) and 101.325 kPa (1.00 atm ; 760 Torr ) .
Natural gas companies in Europe , Australia , and South America have adopted 15 °C (288.15 K ; 59.00 °F ) and 1 atm (101.325 kPa ) as their standard gas volume reference conditions, used as the base values for defining the standard cubic meter .

results.title: Atmospheric pressure - Wikipedia
excerpts:
The standard atmosphere (symbol: atm) is a unit of pressure defined as 101.325 kPa (1,013.25 hPa ) , which is equivalent to 1,013.25 millibars , 760 torr (or about 760 mmHg ), about 29.9212 inHg , or about 14.696 psi .
[ 8 ] This is in contrast to mean sea-level pressure, which involves the extrapolation of pressure to sea level for locations above or below sea level. The average pressure at mean sea level ( MSL ) in the International Standard Atmosphere ( ISA ) is 1,013.25 hPa, or 1 atmosphere (atm), or 29.92 inches of mercury.

[ edit ]
One atmosphere ( 101.325 kPa or 14.7 psi ) is also the pressure caused by the weight of a column of freshwater of approximately 10.3 m (33.8 ft) . Thus, a diver 10.3 m under water experiences a pressure of about 2 atmospheres (1 atm of air plus 1 atm of water).

results.title: atm – Standard Atmosphere Pressure Unit
excerpts:
Standard Atmosphere is mainly used as a reference value for the average atmospheric pressure at sea level. It is often used to indicate the depth rating for a water resistant watch, but otherwise is rarely used as a unit for measuring pressure. 1 standard atmosphere is defined as being exactly equal to 101,325 pascals.
Since the atmospheric pressure varies with changes in weather and altitude, it is convenient to standardise on a single value so that ratings, measurements and specifications can be compared. In particular 1 Standard Atmosphere is used by the Aviation industry as the reference standard for sea level pressure.

What is the average pressure on Earth at sea level in bar pressure?
The internationally accepted ‘standard’ value at sea level is 1.01325 bar.
So 1.01325 bar is not a real average as such, but used more as a sensible value that has been chosen as the representative average pressure for the Earth’s atmosphere at sea level.

results.title: atm to bar — standard atmospheres to bar
excerpts:
For a quick mental estimate, the two units are close enough that the numbers barely change — useful when you only need a rough sense of scale. What does a standard atmosphere actually look like? +
One standard atmosphere is sea-level air pressure by definition. One standard atmosphere is defined as exactly 101,325 pascals.
It is a reference value rather than a measurement of the actual air pressure today. And what is a bar? +
One bar is roughly atmospheric pressure at sea level. One bar is exactly 100,000 pascals, chosen to be close to average atmospheric pressure at sea level. It is the common unit for tyre and diving pressures in Europe. Is this conversion exact? +
How to convert standard atmospheres to bar
Multiply by 1.01325 . One standard atmosphere is1.01325bar, and one baris 0.986923267standard atmospheres.
bar = atm × 1.01325
Worked example
10atm = 10.1325bar . For a sense of scale, one standard atmosphere is sea-level air pressure by definition, and one bar isroughly atmospheric pressure at sea level.
About the standard atmosphere
One standard atmosphere is defined as exactly 101,325 pascals. It is a reference value rather than a measurement of the actual air pressure today.
About the bar
One bar is exactly 100,000 pascals, chosen to be close to average atmospheric pressure at sea level. It is the common unit for tyre and diving pressures in Europe.
